entries.question: What is SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle)?
entries.answer: **SDLC** (Software Development Life Cycle) — Phases to build software: plan → design → build → test → deploy → maintain.
entries.summary: SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle) — Phases to build software: plan → design → build → test → deploy → maintain.

entries.question: What is STLC (Software Testing Life Cycle)?
entries.answer: **STLC** (Software Testing Life Cycle) — Phases of testing: requirement analysis → test plan → test cases → execution → closure.
entries.summary: STLC (Software Testing Life Cycle) — Phases of testing: requirement analysis → test plan → test cases → execution → closure.

entries.question: What is Environment?
entries.answer: **Environment** — A copy of the system for a purpose: DEV, QA/TEST, UAT, STAGING, PROD.
entries.summary: Environment — A copy of the system for a purpose: DEV, QA/TEST, UAT, STAGING, PROD.

entries.question: What is Production (Prod)?
entries.answer: **Production (Prod)** — The live system real users use.
entries.summary: Production (Prod) — The live system real users use.

entries.question: What is UAT (User Acceptance Testing)?
entries.answer: **UAT** (User Acceptance Testing) — Business users confirm the software meets their needs before release.
entries.summary: UAT (User Acceptance Testing) — Business users confirm the software meets their needs before release.

entries.question: What is POC (Proof of Concept)?
entries.answer: **POC** (Proof of Concept) — Small experiment to prove an idea works technically.
entries.summary: POC (Proof of Concept) — Small experiment to prove an idea works technically.

entries.question: What is MVP (Minimum Viable Product)?
entries.answer: **MVP** (Minimum Viable Product) — Smallest usable version of a product released to learn from users.
entries.summary: MVP (Minimum Viable Product) — Smallest usable version of a product released to learn from users.

entries.question: What is Legacy System?
entries.answer: **Legacy System** — Old system still in use, usually hard to change.
entries.summary: Legacy System — Old system still in use, usually hard to change.

entries.question: What is Technical Debt?
entries.answer: **Technical Debt** — Future cost of shortcuts taken today in code or design.
entries.summary: Technical Debt — Future cost of shortcuts taken today in code or design.

entries.question: What is Refactoring?
entries.answer: **Refactoring** — Improving code structure without changing behaviour.
entries.summary: Refactoring — Improving code structure without changing behaviour.

entries.question: What is Version Control / Git?
entries.answer: **Version Control / Git** — Tracks code changes over time. Git is the standard tool.
entries.summary: Version Control / Git — Tracks code changes over time. Git is the standard tool.

entries.question: What is Branch / Merge / PR?
entries.answer: **Branch / Merge / PR** — Branch = separate line of work; PR (Pull Request) = request to merge it after review.
entries.summary: Branch / Merge / PR — Branch = separate line of work; PR (Pull Request) = request to merge it after review.

entries.question: What is IDE (Integrated Development Environment)?
entries.answer: **IDE** (Integrated Development Environment) — Code editor with build/debug tools. E.g. IntelliJ, VS Code, Eclipse.
entries.summary: IDE (Integrated Development Environment) — Code editor with build/debug tools. E.g. IntelliJ, VS Code, Eclipse.

entries.question: What is SDK (Software Development Kit)?
entries.answer: **SDK** (Software Development Kit) — Package of libraries and tools to build for a platform.
entries.summary: SDK (Software Development Kit) — Package of libraries and tools to build for a platform.

entries.question: What is Library vs Framework?
entries.answer: **Library vs Framework** — You call a library; a framework calls your code (inversion of control).
entries.summary: Library vs Framework — You call a library; a framework calls your code (inversion of control).

entries.question: What is Open Source?
entries.answer: **Open Source** — Software with public source code anyone can use under a licence.
entries.summary: Open Source — Software with public source code anyone can use under a licence.

entries.question: What is Hotfix / Patch?
entries.answer: **Hotfix / Patch** — Urgent fix released directly to production.
entries.summary: Hotfix / Patch — Urgent fix released directly to production.

entries.question: What is Semantic Versioning (SemVer)?
entries.answer: **Semantic Versioning** (SemVer) — MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH — breaking.feature.fix (e.g. 2.4.1).
entries.summary: Semantic Versioning (SemVer) — MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH — breaking.feature.fix (e.g. 2.4.1).

entries.question: What is Compiled vs Interpreted?
entries.answer: **Compiled vs Interpreted** — Compiled turns code into machine code before running (C, Go); interpreted runs line by line (Python, JS). Java compiles to bytecode for the JVM.
entries.summary: Compiled vs Interpreted — Compiled turns code into machine code before running (C, Go); interpreted runs line by line (Python, JS). Java compiles to bytecode for the JVM.

entries.question: What is Runtime?
entries.answer: **Runtime** — Environment that executes code: JVM, Node.js, .NET CLR, browser.
entries.summary: Runtime — Environment that executes code: JVM, Node.js, .NET CLR, browser.

entries.question: What is DOM (Document Object Model)?
entries.answer: **DOM** (Document Object Model) — Tree representation of a web page that JavaScript can change.
entries.summary: DOM (Document Object Model) — Tree representation of a web page that JavaScript can change.

entries.question: What is SPA (Single Page Application)?
entries.answer: **SPA** (Single Page Application) — Web app that loads once and updates content without full page reloads (Angular, React).
entries.summary: SPA (Single Page Application) — Web app that loads once and updates content without full page reloads (Angular, React).

entries.question: What is SSR / CSR / SSG?
entries.answer: **SSR / CSR / SSG** — Server-Side Rendering, Client-Side Rendering, Static Site Generation — where/when HTML is built.
entries.summary: SSR / CSR / SSG — Server-Side Rendering, Client-Side Rendering, Static Site Generation — where/when HTML is built.

entries.question: What is Responsive Design?
entries.answer: **Responsive Design** — Layouts that adapt to phone, tablet and desktop screens.
entries.summary: Responsive Design — Layouts that adapt to phone, tablet and desktop screens.

entries.question: What is Component?
entries.answer: **Component** — Reusable UI building block with its own template, style and logic.
entries.summary: Component — Reusable UI building block with its own template, style and logic.

entries.question: What is State Management?
entries.answer: **State Management** — Keeping shared UI data consistent. Tools: NgRx, Redux, Signals, Zustand.
entries.summary: State Management — Keeping shared UI data consistent. Tools: NgRx, Redux, Signals, Zustand.

entries.question: What is Accessibility (a11y)?
entries.answer: **Accessibility (a11y)** — Making apps usable by everyone, including disabled users. Standard: WCAG.
entries.summary: Accessibility (a11y) — Making apps usable by everyone, including disabled users. Standard: WCAG.

entries.question: What is Core Web Vitals?
entries.answer: **Core Web Vitals** — Google page-quality metrics: LCP (load), INP (interactivity), CLS (layout shift).
entries.summary: Core Web Vitals — Google page-quality metrics: LCP (load), INP (interactivity), CLS (layout shift).

entries.question: What is Bundler?
entries.answer: **Bundler** — Combines and optimises JS/CSS files. E.g. Vite, Webpack, esbuild.
entries.summary: Bundler — Combines and optimises JS/CSS files. E.g. Vite, Webpack, esbuild.

entries.question: What is PWA (Progressive Web App)?
entries.answer: **PWA** (Progressive Web App) — Website that works offline and installs like an app.
entries.summary: PWA (Progressive Web App) — Website that works offline and installs like an app.

entries.question: What is Design System?
entries.answer: **Design System** — Shared set of UI components, colours and rules. E.g. Material Design.
entries.summary: Design System — Shared set of UI components, colours and rules. E.g. Material Design.

entries.question: What is Lazy Loading?
entries.answer: **Lazy Loading** — Load code or images only when needed.
entries.summary: Lazy Loading — Load code or images only when needed.

entries.question: What is API (Application Programming Interface)?
entries.answer: **API** (Application Programming Interface) — Contract that lets one program talk to another.
entries.summary: API (Application Programming Interface) — Contract that lets one program talk to another.

entries.question: What is REST (Representational State Transfer)?
entries.answer: **REST** (Representational State Transfer) — API style using HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) on resources/URLs.
entries.summary: REST (Representational State Transfer) — API style using HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) on resources/URLs.

entries.question: What is GraphQL?
entries.answer: **GraphQL** — API query language where clients ask for exactly the fields they need.
entries.summary: GraphQL — API query language where clients ask for exactly the fields they need.

entries.question: What is gRPC?
entries.answer: **gRPC** — Fast binary API protocol using Protocol Buffers; common between microservices.
entries.summary: gRPC — Fast binary API protocol using Protocol Buffers; common between microservices.

entries.question: What is Webhook?
entries.answer: **Webhook** — A server calls your URL when an event happens (push instead of polling).
entries.summary: Webhook — A server calls your URL when an event happens (push instead of polling).

entries.question: What is WebSocket?
entries.answer: **WebSocket** — Two-way live connection for chat, notifications, live data.
entries.summary: WebSocket — Two-way live connection for chat, notifications, live data.

entries.question: What is JSON / XML / YAML?
entries.answer: **JSON / XML / YAML** — Text data formats. JSON for APIs, XML for older systems, YAML for config.
entries.summary: JSON / XML / YAML — Text data formats. JSON for APIs, XML for older systems, YAML for config.

entries.question: What is HTTP Status Codes?
entries.answer: **HTTP Status Codes** — 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error (404, 401), 5xx server error (500).
entries.summary: HTTP Status Codes — 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error (404, 401), 5xx server error (500).

entries.question: What is Endpoint?
entries.answer: **Endpoint** — A specific API URL, e.g. GET /api/orders/42.
entries.summary: Endpoint — A specific API URL, e.g. GET /api/orders/42.

entries.question: What is Middleware?
entries.answer: **Middleware** — Code that runs between request and response (logging, auth) — or software linking systems.
entries.summary: Middleware — Code that runs between request and response (logging, auth) — or software linking systems.

entries.question: What is ORM (Object-Relational Mapping)?
entries.answer: **ORM** (Object-Relational Mapping) — Maps database tables to code objects. E.g. Hibernate/JPA, Entity Framework, Prisma.
entries.summary: ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) — Maps database tables to code objects. E.g. Hibernate/JPA, Entity Framework, Prisma.

entries.question: What is Dependency Injection (DI)?
entries.answer: **Dependency Injection (DI)** — Framework supplies an object's dependencies instead of the object creating them (Spring, Angular).
entries.summary: Dependency Injection (DI) — Framework supplies an object's dependencies instead of the object creating them (Spring, Angular).

entries.question: What is OOP (Object-Oriented Programming)?
entries.answer: **OOP** (Object-Oriented Programming) — Code organised as objects. Pillars: encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism.
entries.summary: OOP (Object-Oriented Programming) — Code organised as objects. Pillars: encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism.

entries.question: What is SOLID?
entries.answer: **SOLID** — Five design principles for maintainable OOP code.
entries.summary: SOLID — Five design principles for maintainable OOP code.

entries.question: What is Design Patterns?
entries.answer: **Design Patterns** — Reusable solutions: Singleton, Factory, Builder, Strategy, Observer, Adapter.
entries.summary: Design Patterns — Reusable solutions: Singleton, Factory, Builder, Strategy, Observer, Adapter.

entries.question: What is Concurrency / Multithreading?
entries.answer: **Concurrency / Multithreading** — Doing multiple tasks at the same time safely.
entries.summary: Concurrency / Multithreading — Doing multiple tasks at the same time safely.

entries.question: What is Idempotency?
entries.answer: **Idempotency** — Repeating the same request gives the same result — e.g. no double payment on retry.
entries.summary: Idempotency — Repeating the same request gives the same result — e.g. no double payment on retry.

entries.question: What is Rate Limiting?
entries.answer: **Rate Limiting** — Capping how many requests a client can make in a time window.
entries.summary: Rate Limiting — Capping how many requests a client can make in a time window.

entries.question: What is Swagger / OpenAPI?
entries.answer: **Swagger / OpenAPI** — Standard to describe and document REST APIs.
entries.summary: Swagger / OpenAPI — Standard to describe and document REST APIs.

entries.question: What is Big-O Notation?
entries.answer: **Big-O Notation** — How work grows with input size: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²).
entries.summary: Big-O Notation — How work grows with input size: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²).

entries.question: What is DSA (Data Structures & Algorithms)?
entries.answer: **DSA** (Data Structures & Algorithms) — Arrays, lists, maps, trees, graphs + sorting/searching techniques.
entries.summary: DSA (Data Structures & Algorithms) — Arrays, lists, maps, trees, graphs + sorting/searching techniques.

entries.question: What is Monolith?
entries.answer: **Monolith** — Whole application built and deployed as one unit.
entries.summary: Monolith — Whole application built and deployed as one unit.

entries.question: What is Microservices?
entries.answer: **Microservices** — System split into small, independently deployable services.
entries.summary: Microservices — System split into small, independently deployable services.

entries.question: What is Modular Monolith?
entries.answer: **Modular Monolith** — One deployable app with strict internal module boundaries.
entries.summary: Modular Monolith — One deployable app with strict internal module boundaries.

entries.question: What is Serverless?
entries.answer: **Serverless** — Run code without managing servers; pay per use. E.g. AWS Lambda, Azure Functions.
entries.summary: Serverless — Run code without managing servers; pay per use. E.g. AWS Lambda, Azure Functions.

entries.question: What is Event-Driven Architecture?
entries.answer: **Event-Driven Architecture** — Services react to events via a broker (Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS).
entries.summary: Event-Driven Architecture — Services react to events via a broker (Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS).

entries.question: What is Message Queue / Broker?
entries.answer: **Message Queue / Broker** — Holds messages between services for async processing. E.g. Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS.
entries.summary: Message Queue / Broker — Holds messages between services for async processing. E.g. Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS.

entries.question: What is API Gateway?
entries.answer: **API Gateway** — Single entry point that routes, authenticates and rate-limits API calls.
entries.summary: API Gateway — Single entry point that routes, authenticates and rate-limits API calls.

entries.question: What is Load Balancer?
entries.answer: **Load Balancer** — Spreads traffic across multiple servers.
entries.summary: Load Balancer — Spreads traffic across multiple servers.

entries.question: What is Caching?
entries.answer: **Caching** — Storing frequent data in fast memory. E.g. Redis, CDN.
entries.summary: Caching — Storing frequent data in fast memory. E.g. Redis, CDN.

entries.question: What is CDN (Content Delivery Network)?
entries.answer: **CDN** (Content Delivery Network) — Servers worldwide that deliver static content close to users. E.g. CloudFront, Cloudflare.
entries.summary: CDN (Content Delivery Network) — Servers worldwide that deliver static content close to users. E.g. CloudFront, Cloudflare.

entries.question: What is Scalability (Horizontal / Vertical)?
entries.answer: **Scalability (Horizontal / Vertical)** — Handle more load by adding machines (horizontal) or bigger machines (vertical).
entries.summary: Scalability (Horizontal / Vertical) — Handle more load by adding machines (horizontal) or bigger machines (vertical).

entries.question: What is High Availability (HA)?
entries.answer: **High Availability (HA)** — System stays up despite failures, often measured as 99.9% uptime.
entries.summary: High Availability (HA) — System stays up despite failures, often measured as 99.9% uptime.

entries.question: What is Fault Tolerance / Resilience?
entries.answer: **Fault Tolerance / Resilience** — Keep working when parts fail: retries, timeouts, circuit breakers.
entries.summary: Fault Tolerance / Resilience — Keep working when parts fail: retries, timeouts, circuit breakers.

entries.question: What is Circuit Breaker?
entries.answer: **Circuit Breaker** — Stops calling a failing service for a while to prevent cascade failures.
entries.summary: Circuit Breaker — Stops calling a failing service for a while to prevent cascade failures.

entries.question: What is CAP Theorem?
entries.answer: **CAP Theorem** — A distributed system can guarantee only two of: Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance.
entries.summary: CAP Theorem — A distributed system can guarantee only two of: Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance.

entries.question: What is Saga Pattern?
entries.answer: **Saga Pattern** — Manages a multi-service transaction as steps with compensating actions.
entries.summary: Saga Pattern — Manages a multi-service transaction as steps with compensating actions.

entries.question: What is CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)?
entries.answer: **CQRS** (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) — Separate models for writing and reading data.
entries.summary: CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) — Separate models for writing and reading data.

entries.question: What is DDD (Domain-Driven Design)?
entries.answer: **DDD** (Domain-Driven Design) — Design software around business domains and their language.
entries.summary: DDD (Domain-Driven Design) — Design software around business domains and their language.

entries.question: What is Hexagonal / Clean Architecture?
entries.answer: **Hexagonal / Clean Architecture** — Keep business logic independent of frameworks, UI and databases.
entries.summary: Hexagonal / Clean Architecture — Keep business logic independent of frameworks, UI and databases.

entries.question: What is Service Mesh?
entries.answer: **Service Mesh** — Infrastructure layer handling service-to-service traffic, security and metrics. E.g. Istio.
entries.summary: Service Mesh — Infrastructure layer handling service-to-service traffic, security and metrics. E.g. Istio.

entries.question: What is Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs)?
entries.answer: **Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs)** — Qualities like performance, security, scalability, availability — not features.
entries.summary: Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs) — Qualities like performance, security, scalability, availability — not features.

entries.question: What is ADR (Architecture Decision Record)?
entries.answer: **ADR** (Architecture Decision Record) — Short document recording a design decision and why.
entries.summary: ADR (Architecture Decision Record) — Short document recording a design decision and why.

entries.question: What is RDBMS / SQL?
entries.answer: **RDBMS / SQL** — Table-based databases queried with SQL. E.g. PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server.
entries.summary: RDBMS / SQL — Table-based databases queried with SQL. E.g. PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server.

entries.question: What is NoSQL?
entries.answer: **NoSQL** — Non-table databases: document (MongoDB), key-value (Redis, DynamoDB), column (Cassandra), graph (Neo4j).
entries.summary: NoSQL — Non-table databases: document (MongoDB), key-value (Redis, DynamoDB), column (Cassandra), graph (Neo4j).

entries.question: What is ACID?
entries.answer: **ACID** — Transaction guarantees: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.
entries.summary: ACID — Transaction guarantees: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.

entries.question: What is Transaction?
entries.answer: **Transaction** — Group of DB operations that all succeed or all fail.
entries.summary: Transaction — Group of DB operations that all succeed or all fail.

entries.question: What is Index?
entries.answer: **Index** — Data structure that speeds up lookups, like a book index.
entries.summary: Index — Data structure that speeds up lookups, like a book index.

entries.question: What is Normalization?
entries.answer: **Normalization** — Organising tables to avoid duplicate data.
entries.summary: Normalization — Organising tables to avoid duplicate data.

entries.question: What is Primary / Foreign Key?
entries.answer: **Primary / Foreign Key** — Primary key uniquely identifies a row; foreign key links to another table.
entries.summary: Primary / Foreign Key — Primary key uniquely identifies a row; foreign key links to another table.

entries.question: What is Join?
entries.answer: **Join** — Combines rows from tables: INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL.
entries.summary: Join — Combines rows from tables: INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL.

entries.question: What is Stored Procedure?
entries.answer: **Stored Procedure** — Saved SQL program that runs inside the database.
entries.summary: Stored Procedure — Saved SQL program that runs inside the database.

entries.question: What is Sharding / Partitioning?
entries.answer: **Sharding / Partitioning** — Splitting data across machines or segments to scale.
entries.summary: Sharding / Partitioning — Splitting data across machines or segments to scale.

entries.question: What is Replication?
entries.answer: **Replication** — Copying data to other servers for availability and read scaling.
entries.summary: Replication — Copying data to other servers for availability and read scaling.

entries.question: What is ETL / ELT?
entries.answer: **ETL / ELT** — Extract, Transform, Load — moving data into a warehouse (ELT transforms after loading).
entries.summary: ETL / ELT — Extract, Transform, Load — moving data into a warehouse (ELT transforms after loading).

entries.question: What is Data Warehouse?
entries.answer: **Data Warehouse** — Structured store for analytics. E.g. Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift.
entries.summary: Data Warehouse — Structured store for analytics. E.g. Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift.

entries.question: What is Data Lake / Lakehouse?
entries.answer: **Data Lake / Lakehouse** — Store of raw data in any format (lake); lakehouse adds warehouse features. E.g. Databricks.
entries.summary: Data Lake / Lakehouse — Store of raw data in any format (lake); lakehouse adds warehouse features. E.g. Databricks.

entries.question: What is Data Pipeline?
entries.answer: **Data Pipeline** — Automated flow that moves and transforms data.
entries.summary: Data Pipeline — Automated flow that moves and transforms data.

entries.question: What is Batch vs Streaming?
entries.answer: **Batch vs Streaming** — Process data in scheduled chunks vs continuously in real time.
entries.summary: Batch vs Streaming — Process data in scheduled chunks vs continuously in real time.

entries.question: What is Big Data?
entries.answer: **Big Data** — Data too large/fast for one machine. Tools: Spark, Hadoop, Kafka.
entries.summary: Big Data — Data too large/fast for one machine. Tools: Spark, Hadoop, Kafka.

entries.question: What is OLTP vs OLAP?
entries.answer: **OLTP vs OLAP** — OLTP = day-to-day transactions; OLAP = analytics and reporting.
entries.summary: OLTP vs OLAP — OLTP = day-to-day transactions; OLAP = analytics and reporting.

entries.question: What is BI (Business Intelligence)?
entries.answer: **BI** (Business Intelligence) — Dashboards and reports for business decisions. E.g. Power BI, Tableau.
entries.summary: BI (Business Intelligence) — Dashboards and reports for business decisions. E.g. Power BI, Tableau.

entries.question: What is Schema Migration?
entries.answer: **Schema Migration** — Versioned DB structure changes. Tools: Flyway, Liquibase.
entries.summary: Schema Migration — Versioned DB structure changes. Tools: Flyway, Liquibase.

entries.question: What is Cloud Computing?
entries.answer: **Cloud Computing** — Renting computing resources over the internet. Big 3: AWS, Azure, GCP.
entries.summary: Cloud Computing — Renting computing resources over the internet. Big 3: AWS, Azure, GCP.

entries.question: What is IaaS / PaaS / SaaS?
entries.answer: **IaaS / PaaS / SaaS** — Infrastructure (EC2), Platform (Heroku, App Service), Software (Gmail, Salesforce) as a Service.
entries.summary: IaaS / PaaS / SaaS — Infrastructure (EC2), Platform (Heroku, App Service), Software (Gmail, Salesforce) as a Service.

entries.question: What is Public / Private / Hybrid Cloud?
entries.answer: **Public / Private / Hybrid Cloud** — Shared provider cloud / company-only cloud / mix of both.
entries.summary: Public / Private / Hybrid Cloud — Shared provider cloud / company-only cloud / mix of both.

entries.question: What is Region / Availability Zone?
entries.answer: **Region / Availability Zone** — Region = geographic area; AZ = isolated data centre within it.
entries.summary: Region / Availability Zone — Region = geographic area; AZ = isolated data centre within it.

entries.question: What is VM (Virtual Machine)?
entries.answer: **VM** (Virtual Machine) — Software-emulated computer running its own OS.
entries.summary: VM (Virtual Machine) — Software-emulated computer running its own OS.

entries.question: What is Container / Docker?
entries.answer: **Container / Docker** — Lightweight package of an app and its dependencies that runs anywhere.
entries.summary: Container / Docker — Lightweight package of an app and its dependencies that runs anywhere.

entries.question: What is Kubernetes (K8s)?
entries.answer: **Kubernetes (K8s)** — Runs and scales containers across many machines. Terms: pod, deployment, service.
entries.summary: Kubernetes (K8s) — Runs and scales containers across many machines. Terms: pod, deployment, service.

entries.question: What is DevOps?
entries.answer: **DevOps** — Culture and practices joining development and operations to ship faster and safer.
entries.summary: DevOps — Culture and practices joining development and operations to ship faster and safer.

entries.question: What is CI/CD?
entries.answer: **CI/CD** — Continuous Integration (auto build+test) and Continuous Delivery/Deployment (auto release).
entries.summary: CI/CD — Continuous Integration (auto build+test) and Continuous Delivery/Deployment (auto release).

entries.question: What is Pipeline?
entries.answer: **Pipeline** — Automated steps: build → test → scan → deploy. E.g. Jenkins, GitHub Actions.
entries.summary: Pipeline — Automated steps: build → test → scan → deploy. E.g. Jenkins, GitHub Actions.

entries.question: What is IaC (Infrastructure as Code)?
entries.answer: **IaC** (Infrastructure as Code) — Define servers and networks in code files. E.g. Terraform, CloudFormation.
entries.summary: IaC (Infrastructure as Code) — Define servers and networks in code files. E.g. Terraform, CloudFormation.

entries.question: What is Configuration Management?
entries.answer: **Configuration Management** — Automate server setup. E.g. Ansible, Chef, Puppet.
entries.summary: Configuration Management — Automate server setup. E.g. Ansible, Chef, Puppet.

entries.question: What is GitOps?
entries.answer: **GitOps** — Git is the source of truth for deployments. E.g. Argo CD, Flux.
entries.summary: GitOps — Git is the source of truth for deployments. E.g. Argo CD, Flux.

entries.question: What is Blue-Green / Canary Deployment?
entries.answer: **Blue-Green / Canary Deployment** — Release strategies: switch between two environments / release to a small % first.
entries.summary: Blue-Green / Canary Deployment — Release strategies: switch between two environments / release to a small % first.

entries.question: What is Feature Flag?
entries.answer: **Feature Flag** — Turn features on/off without redeploying.
entries.summary: Feature Flag — Turn features on/off without redeploying.

entries.question: What is Observability?
entries.answer: **Observability** — Understand system state via logs, metrics and traces. Tools: Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry.
entries.summary: Observability — Understand system state via logs, metrics and traces. Tools: Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry.

entries.question: What is SLA / SLO / SLI?
entries.answer: **SLA / SLO / SLI** — Agreement with customer / internal target / actual measurement (e.g. 99.9% uptime).
entries.summary: SLA / SLO / SLI — Agreement with customer / internal target / actual measurement (e.g. 99.9% uptime).

entries.question: What is Auto Scaling?
entries.answer: **Auto Scaling** — Automatically add/remove servers based on load.
entries.summary: Auto Scaling — Automatically add/remove servers based on load.

entries.question: What is FinOps?
entries.answer: **FinOps** — Managing and reducing cloud costs.
entries.summary: FinOps — Managing and reducing cloud costs.

entries.question: What is Artifact / Registry?
entries.answer: **Artifact / Registry** — Built output (JAR, Docker image) stored in a repo like Nexus, Artifactory, ECR.
entries.summary: Artifact / Registry — Built output (JAR, Docker image) stored in a repo like Nexus, Artifactory, ECR.

entries.question: What is AI (Artificial Intelligence)?
entries.answer: **AI** (Artificial Intelligence) — Machines performing tasks that need human-like intelligence.
entries.summary: AI (Artificial Intelligence) — Machines performing tasks that need human-like intelligence.

entries.question: What is Machine Learning (ML)?
entries.answer: **Machine Learning (ML)** — Systems learn patterns from data instead of hard-coded rules.
entries.summary: Machine Learning (ML) — Systems learn patterns from data instead of hard-coded rules.

entries.question: What is Deep Learning?
entries.answer: **Deep Learning** — ML using multi-layer neural networks; powers vision, speech and LLMs.
entries.summary: Deep Learning — ML using multi-layer neural networks; powers vision, speech and LLMs.

entries.question: What is Supervised / Unsupervised Learning?
entries.answer: **Supervised / Unsupervised Learning** — Learn from labelled examples / find patterns in unlabelled data.
entries.summary: Supervised / Unsupervised Learning — Learn from labelled examples / find patterns in unlabelled data.

entries.question: What is Model / Training / Inference?
entries.answer: **Model / Training / Inference** — Model = learned function; training = learning it; inference = using it to predict.
entries.summary: Model / Training / Inference — Model = learned function; training = learning it; inference = using it to predict.

entries.question: What is Generative AI (GenAI)?
entries.answer: **Generative AI (GenAI)** — AI that creates text, images, code or audio.
entries.summary: Generative AI (GenAI) — AI that creates text, images, code or audio.

entries.question: What is LLM (Large Language Model)?
entries.answer: **LLM** (Large Language Model) — Model trained on huge text to understand and generate language. E.g. Claude, GPT, Gemini, Llama.
entries.summary: LLM (Large Language Model) — Model trained on huge text to understand and generate language. E.g. Claude, GPT, Gemini, Llama.

entries.question: What is Token / Context Window?
entries.answer: **Token / Context Window** — Token = chunk of text a model reads; context window = max tokens it can consider at once.
entries.summary: Token / Context Window — Token = chunk of text a model reads; context window = max tokens it can consider at once.

entries.question: What is Prompt Engineering?
entries.answer: **Prompt Engineering** — Writing clear instructions and examples to get better model output.
entries.summary: Prompt Engineering — Writing clear instructions and examples to get better model output.

entries.question: What is Embedding?
entries.answer: **Embedding** — Numeric vector representing meaning of text, used for similarity search.
entries.summary: Embedding — Numeric vector representing meaning of text, used for similarity search.

entries.question: What is Vector Database?
entries.answer: **Vector Database** — Stores embeddings for semantic search. E.g. pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate.
entries.summary: Vector Database — Stores embeddings for semantic search. E.g. pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate.

entries.question: What is RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)?
entries.answer: **RAG** (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) — Fetch relevant documents first, then let the LLM answer using them.
entries.summary: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) — Fetch relevant documents first, then let the LLM answer using them.

entries.question: What is Fine-tuning?
entries.answer: **Fine-tuning** — Further training a model on specific data for a task.
entries.summary: Fine-tuning — Further training a model on specific data for a task.

entries.question: What is Hallucination?
entries.answer: **Hallucination** — When a model confidently generates incorrect information.
entries.summary: Hallucination — When a model confidently generates incorrect information.

entries.question: What is AI Agent?
entries.answer: **AI Agent** — LLM that plans and uses tools in steps to complete a task.
entries.summary: AI Agent — LLM that plans and uses tools in steps to complete a task.

entries.question: What is Tool / Function Calling?
entries.answer: **Tool / Function Calling** — Model requests a defined function/API call with structured arguments.
entries.summary: Tool / Function Calling — Model requests a defined function/API call with structured arguments.

entries.question: What is MCP (Model Context Protocol)?
entries.answer: **MCP** (Model Context Protocol) — Open standard for connecting AI apps to tools and data sources.
entries.summary: MCP (Model Context Protocol) — Open standard for connecting AI apps to tools and data sources.

entries.question: What is Guardrails?
entries.answer: **Guardrails** — Rules and checks that keep AI output safe and on-topic.
entries.summary: Guardrails — Rules and checks that keep AI output safe and on-topic.

entries.question: What is MLOps / LLMOps?
entries.answer: **MLOps / LLMOps** — Practices to deploy, monitor and update ML/LLM systems in production.
entries.summary: MLOps / LLMOps — Practices to deploy, monitor and update ML/LLM systems in production.

entries.question: What is NLP / Computer Vision?
entries.answer: **NLP / Computer Vision** — AI for language / AI for images and video.
entries.summary: NLP / Computer Vision — AI for language / AI for images and video.

entries.question: What is Agentic AI?
entries.answer: **Agentic AI** — AI systems that act on their own — plan, use tools and take multi-step actions toward a goal.
entries.summary: Agentic AI — AI systems that act on their own — plan, use tools and take multi-step actions toward a goal.

entries.question: What is Multi-Agent System?
entries.answer: **Multi-Agent System** — Several specialised agents cooperating (e.g. planner, researcher, coder).
entries.summary: Multi-Agent System — Several specialised agents cooperating (e.g. planner, researcher, coder).

entries.question: What is Context Engineering?
entries.answer: **Context Engineering** — Choosing what instructions, data, tools and memory go into a model's context window.
entries.summary: Context Engineering — Choosing what instructions, data, tools and memory go into a model's context window.

entries.question: What is Evals (Evaluations)?
entries.answer: **Evals** (Evaluations) — Automated tests that score AI output quality before and after changes.
entries.summary: Evals (Evaluations) — Automated tests that score AI output quality before and after changes.

entries.question: What is LLM-as-a-Judge?
entries.answer: **LLM-as-a-Judge** — Using one model to grade another model's answers.
entries.summary: LLM-as-a-Judge — Using one model to grade another model's answers.

entries.question: What is Grounding?
entries.answer: **Grounding** — Tying AI answers to trusted sources to reduce hallucination.
entries.summary: Grounding — Tying AI answers to trusted sources to reduce hallucination.

entries.question: What is Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)?
entries.answer: **Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)** — A person reviews or approves AI actions at key steps.
entries.summary: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) — A person reviews or approves AI actions at key steps.

entries.question: What is Prompt Injection / Jailbreak?
entries.answer: **Prompt Injection / Jailbreak** — Malicious text that tricks a model into ignoring its rules / bypassing safety.
entries.summary: Prompt Injection / Jailbreak — Malicious text that tricks a model into ignoring its rules / bypassing safety.

entries.question: What is Foundation Model?
entries.answer: **Foundation Model** — Large general-purpose model adapted to many tasks (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Llama).
entries.summary: Foundation Model — Large general-purpose model adapted to many tasks (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Llama).

entries.question: What is Multimodal?
entries.answer: **Multimodal** — Model that handles text, images, audio and/or video together.
entries.summary: Multimodal — Model that handles text, images, audio and/or video together.

entries.question: What is Reasoning Model?
entries.answer: **Reasoning Model** — Model that 'thinks' step by step before answering, for harder problems.
entries.summary: Reasoning Model — Model that 'thinks' step by step before answering, for harder problems.

entries.question: What is SLM (Small Language Model)?
entries.answer: **SLM** (Small Language Model) — Compact model that runs cheaply or on-device (Phi, Gemma, Llama small).
entries.summary: SLM (Small Language Model) — Compact model that runs cheaply or on-device (Phi, Gemma, Llama small).

entries.question: What is Open-Weight Model?
entries.answer: **Open-Weight Model** — Model whose weights are downloadable to self-host (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek).
entries.summary: Open-Weight Model — Model whose weights are downloadable to self-host (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek).

entries.question: What is Temperature?
entries.answer: **Temperature** — Setting controlling randomness: low = focused, high = creative.
entries.summary: Temperature — Setting controlling randomness: low = focused, high = creative.

entries.question: What is Structured Output?
entries.answer: **Structured Output** — Forcing the model to return valid JSON matching a schema.
entries.summary: Structured Output — Forcing the model to return valid JSON matching a schema.

entries.question: What is RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback)?
entries.answer: **RLHF** (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) — Training models using human ratings of their answers.
entries.summary: RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) — Training models using human ratings of their answers.

entries.question: What is LoRA / PEFT?
entries.answer: **LoRA / PEFT** — Cheap fine-tuning methods that train only small added weights.
entries.summary: LoRA / PEFT — Cheap fine-tuning methods that train only small added weights.

entries.question: What is Quantization?
entries.answer: **Quantization** — Shrinking model precision (e.g. 16-bit → 4-bit) to run faster on less memory.
entries.summary: Quantization — Shrinking model precision (e.g. 16-bit → 4-bit) to run faster on less memory.

entries.question: What is Distillation?
entries.answer: **Distillation** — Training a small model to copy a large model's behaviour.
entries.summary: Distillation — Training a small model to copy a large model's behaviour.

entries.question: What is MoE (Mixture of Experts)?
entries.answer: **MoE** (Mixture of Experts) — Model architecture that activates only some sub-networks per token for efficiency.
entries.summary: MoE (Mixture of Experts) — Model architecture that activates only some sub-networks per token for efficiency.

entries.question: What is Inference Serving / GPU?
entries.answer: **Inference Serving / GPU** — Running models for users on GPUs; tools: vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Ollama.
entries.summary: Inference Serving / GPU — Running models for users on GPUs; tools: vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Ollama.

entries.question: What is TTFT / Tokens per Second?
entries.answer: **TTFT / Tokens per Second** — Time-to-first-token and generation speed — key LLM latency metrics.
entries.summary: TTFT / Tokens per Second — Time-to-first-token and generation speed — key LLM latency metrics.

entries.question: What is Semantic Caching?
entries.answer: **Semantic Caching** — Reusing answers for similar (not identical) questions to save cost.
entries.summary: Semantic Caching — Reusing answers for similar (not identical) questions to save cost.

entries.question: What is Model Router / AI Gateway?
entries.answer: **Model Router / AI Gateway** — Layer that picks a model per request and handles keys, limits and logging (e.g. LiteLLM).
entries.summary: Model Router / AI Gateway — Layer that picks a model per request and handles keys, limits and logging (e.g. LiteLLM).

entries.question: What is A2A (Agent-to-Agent Protocol)?
entries.answer: **A2A** (Agent-to-Agent Protocol) — Open protocol for agents from different vendors to communicate.
entries.summary: A2A (Agent-to-Agent Protocol) — Open protocol for agents from different vendors to communicate.

entries.question: What is AI Copilot / Assistant?
entries.answer: **AI Copilot / Assistant** — AI embedded in a tool to help a human (GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot).
entries.summary: AI Copilot / Assistant — AI embedded in a tool to help a human (GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot).

entries.question: What is Vibe Coding?
entries.answer: **Vibe Coding** — Building software mainly by prompting AI and accepting its code with light review.
entries.summary: Vibe Coding — Building software mainly by prompting AI and accepting its code with light review.

entries.question: What is Spec-Driven Development?
entries.answer: **Spec-Driven Development** — Writing clear specs first so AI coding agents can implement them reliably.
entries.summary: Spec-Driven Development — Writing clear specs first so AI coding agents can implement them reliably.

entries.question: What is Synthetic Data?
entries.answer: **Synthetic Data** — Artificially generated data used for training or testing.
entries.summary: Synthetic Data — Artificially generated data used for training or testing.

entries.question: What is Edge AI / TinyML?
entries.answer: **Edge AI / TinyML** — Running AI on devices (phones, sensors) instead of the cloud.
entries.summary: Edge AI / TinyML — Running AI on devices (phones, sensors) instead of the cloud.

entries.question: What is Responsible AI?
entries.answer: **Responsible AI** — Building AI that is fair, transparent, private, safe and accountable.
entries.summary: Responsible AI — Building AI that is fair, transparent, private, safe and accountable.

entries.question: What is EU AI Act / ISO 42001?
entries.answer: **EU AI Act / ISO 42001** — EU law classifying AI by risk / international AI management-system standard.
entries.summary: EU AI Act / ISO 42001 — EU law classifying AI by risk / international AI management-system standard.

entries.question: What is AGI (Artificial General Intelligence)?
entries.answer: **AGI** (Artificial General Intelligence) — Hypothetical AI matching humans across most tasks.
entries.summary: AGI (Artificial General Intelligence) — Hypothetical AI matching humans across most tasks.

entries.question: What is Unit Test?
entries.answer: **Unit Test** — Tests one function/class in isolation. E.g. JUnit, Jest, pytest.
entries.summary: Unit Test — Tests one function/class in isolation. E.g. JUnit, Jest, pytest.

entries.question: What is Integration Test?
entries.answer: **Integration Test** — Tests components working together (API + DB).
entries.summary: Integration Test — Tests components working together (API + DB).

entries.question: What is E2E Test (End-to-End)?
entries.answer: **E2E Test** (End-to-End) — Tests a full user journey in a real browser. E.g. Playwright, Cypress, Selenium.
entries.summary: E2E Test (End-to-End) — Tests a full user journey in a real browser. E.g. Playwright, Cypress, Selenium.

entries.question: What is Regression Test?
entries.answer: **Regression Test** — Re-tests old features to ensure new changes didn't break them.
entries.summary: Regression Test — Re-tests old features to ensure new changes didn't break them.

entries.question: What is Smoke / Sanity Test?
entries.answer: **Smoke / Sanity Test** — Quick check that the main features work after a build/deploy.
entries.summary: Smoke / Sanity Test — Quick check that the main features work after a build/deploy.

entries.question: What is Performance / Load Test?
entries.answer: **Performance / Load Test** — Measures speed and stability under traffic. E.g. JMeter, k6.
entries.summary: Performance / Load Test — Measures speed and stability under traffic. E.g. JMeter, k6.

entries.question: What is TDD / BDD?
entries.answer: **TDD / BDD** — Test-Driven Dev (write test first) / Behaviour-Driven Dev (Given-When-Then, Cucumber).
entries.summary: TDD / BDD — Test-Driven Dev (write test first) / Behaviour-Driven Dev (Given-When-Then, Cucumber).

entries.question: What is Mocking?
entries.answer: **Mocking** — Fake dependencies in tests. E.g. Mockito, Jest mocks.
entries.summary: Mocking — Fake dependencies in tests. E.g. Mockito, Jest mocks.

entries.question: What is Code Coverage?
entries.answer: **Code Coverage** — % of code executed by tests. Tools: JaCoCo, Istanbul.
entries.summary: Code Coverage — % of code executed by tests. Tools: JaCoCo, Istanbul.

entries.question: What is Static Code Analysis?
entries.answer: **Static Code Analysis** — Finds bugs/smells without running code. E.g. SonarQube, ESLint.
entries.summary: Static Code Analysis — Finds bugs/smells without running code. E.g. SonarQube, ESLint.

entries.question: What is Code Review?
entries.answer: **Code Review** — Teammates check code before it is merged.
entries.summary: Code Review — Teammates check code before it is merged.

entries.question: What is Bug / Defect Severity vs Priority?
entries.answer: **Bug / Defect Severity vs Priority** — Severity = impact on system; priority = how soon to fix.
entries.summary: Bug / Defect Severity vs Priority — Severity = impact on system; priority = how soon to fix.

entries.question: What is Authentication (AuthN)?
entries.answer: **Authentication (AuthN)** — Verifying who you are (login, password, MFA).
entries.summary: Authentication (AuthN) — Verifying who you are (login, password, MFA).

entries.question: What is Authorization (AuthZ)?
entries.answer: **Authorization (AuthZ)** — Deciding what you are allowed to do.
entries.summary: Authorization (AuthZ) — Deciding what you are allowed to do.

entries.question: What is OAuth 2.0 / OIDC?
entries.answer: **OAuth 2.0 / OIDC** — Standards for delegated access (OAuth) and login identity (OpenID Connect).
entries.summary: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC — Standards for delegated access (OAuth) and login identity (OpenID Connect).

entries.question: What is JWT (JSON Web Token)?
entries.answer: **JWT** (JSON Web Token) — Signed token carrying user identity/claims between systems.
entries.summary: JWT (JSON Web Token) — Signed token carrying user identity/claims between systems.

entries.question: What is SSO (Single Sign-On)?
entries.answer: **SSO** (Single Sign-On) — Log in once to access many apps. E.g. Okta, Entra ID.
entries.summary: SSO (Single Sign-On) — Log in once to access many apps. E.g. Okta, Entra ID.

entries.question: What is MFA / 2FA?
entries.answer: **MFA / 2FA** — Multi-factor authentication: password + phone/app/key.
entries.summary: MFA / 2FA — Multi-factor authentication: password + phone/app/key.

entries.question: What is RBAC (Role-Based Access Control)?
entries.answer: **RBAC** (Role-Based Access Control) — Permissions assigned by role (admin, editor, viewer).
entries.summary: RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) — Permissions assigned by role (admin, editor, viewer).

entries.question: What is Encryption (at rest / in transit)?
entries.answer: **Encryption (at rest / in transit)** — Scrambling data on disk / over the network (TLS/HTTPS).
entries.summary: Encryption (at rest / in transit) — Scrambling data on disk / over the network (TLS/HTTPS).

entries.question: What is Hashing?
entries.answer: **Hashing** — One-way conversion used to store passwords safely (bcrypt, SHA-256).
entries.summary: Hashing — One-way conversion used to store passwords safely (bcrypt, SHA-256).

entries.question: What is OWASP Top 10?
entries.answer: **OWASP Top 10** — Most critical web app risks: injection, broken access control, XSS, etc.
entries.summary: OWASP Top 10 — Most critical web app risks: injection, broken access control, XSS, etc.

entries.question: What is SQL Injection / XSS / CSRF?
entries.answer: **SQL Injection / XSS / CSRF** — Common attacks: malicious SQL input / injected scripts / forged requests.
entries.summary: SQL Injection / XSS / CSRF — Common attacks: malicious SQL input / injected scripts / forged requests.

entries.question: What is Firewall / WAF?
entries.answer: **Firewall / WAF** — Blocks unwanted network traffic / web-specific attacks.
entries.summary: Firewall / WAF — Blocks unwanted network traffic / web-specific attacks.

entries.question: What is Zero Trust?
entries.answer: **Zero Trust** — Never trust by default; verify every user and device every time.
entries.summary: Zero Trust — Never trust by default; verify every user and device every time.

entries.question: What is Vulnerability / CVE?
entries.answer: **Vulnerability / CVE** — Security weakness / its public ID (e.g. CVE-2021-44228 Log4Shell).
entries.summary: Vulnerability / CVE — Security weakness / its public ID (e.g. CVE-2021-44228 Log4Shell).

entries.question: What is SAST / DAST?
entries.answer: **SAST / DAST** — Static (code) / Dynamic (running app) security testing.
entries.summary: SAST / DAST — Static (code) / Dynamic (running app) security testing.

entries.question: What is Secrets Management?
entries.answer: **Secrets Management** — Store passwords/keys safely. E.g. HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager.
entries.summary: Secrets Management — Store passwords/keys safely. E.g. HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager.

entries.question: What is SIEM / SOC?
entries.answer: **SIEM / SOC** — Security log analysis platform (Splunk) / team that monitors threats.
entries.summary: SIEM / SOC — Security log analysis platform (Splunk) / team that monitors threats.

entries.question: What is Penetration Testing?
entries.answer: **Penetration Testing** — Authorised simulated attack to find weaknesses.
entries.summary: Penetration Testing — Authorised simulated attack to find weaknesses.

entries.question: What is IP Address?
entries.answer: **IP Address** — Unique address of a device on a network (IPv4/IPv6).
entries.summary: IP Address — Unique address of a device on a network (IPv4/IPv6).

entries.question: What is DNS (Domain Name System)?
entries.answer: **DNS** (Domain Name System) — Translates names like google.com into IP addresses.
entries.summary: DNS (Domain Name System) — Translates names like google.com into IP addresses.

entries.question: What is HTTP / HTTPS?
entries.answer: **HTTP / HTTPS** — Web protocol; HTTPS is encrypted with TLS.
entries.summary: HTTP / HTTPS — Web protocol; HTTPS is encrypted with TLS.

entries.question: What is TCP / UDP?
entries.answer: **TCP / UDP** — Reliable ordered delivery / fast delivery without guarantees (video, gaming).
entries.summary: TCP / UDP — Reliable ordered delivery / fast delivery without guarantees (video, gaming).

entries.question: What is Port?
entries.answer: **Port** — Numbered channel on a machine: 80 HTTP, 443 HTTPS, 22 SSH, 5432 PostgreSQL.
entries.summary: Port — Numbered channel on a machine: 80 HTTP, 443 HTTPS, 22 SSH, 5432 PostgreSQL.

entries.question: What is VPN (Virtual Private Network)?
entries.answer: **VPN** (Virtual Private Network) — Encrypted tunnel into a private network.
entries.summary: VPN (Virtual Private Network) — Encrypted tunnel into a private network.

entries.question: What is VPC / Subnet?
entries.answer: **VPC / Subnet** — Private cloud network / smaller segment of it (public or private).
entries.summary: VPC / Subnet — Private cloud network / smaller segment of it (public or private).

entries.question: What is Proxy / Reverse Proxy?
entries.answer: **Proxy / Reverse Proxy** — Forwards client requests out / receives requests for servers (Nginx).
entries.summary: Proxy / Reverse Proxy — Forwards client requests out / receives requests for servers (Nginx).

entries.question: What is Latency / Bandwidth / Throughput?
entries.answer: **Latency / Bandwidth / Throughput** — Delay / max capacity / actual data moved per second.
entries.summary: Latency / Bandwidth / Throughput — Delay / max capacity / actual data moved per second.

entries.question: What is OSI Model?
entries.answer: **OSI Model** — 7 network layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.
entries.summary: OSI Model — 7 network layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.

entries.question: What is SSH (Secure Shell)?
entries.answer: **SSH** (Secure Shell) — Encrypted remote login to servers.
entries.summary: SSH (Secure Shell) — Encrypted remote login to servers.

entries.question: What is Agile?
entries.answer: **Agile** — Deliver in small iterations with frequent feedback.
entries.summary: Agile — Deliver in small iterations with frequent feedback.

entries.question: What is Waterfall?
entries.answer: **Waterfall** — Sequential phases; each finishes before the next starts.
entries.summary: Waterfall — Sequential phases; each finishes before the next starts.

entries.question: What is Scrum?
entries.answer: **Scrum** — Agile framework with sprints, roles (PO, SM, Dev team) and ceremonies.
entries.summary: Scrum — Agile framework with sprints, roles (PO, SM, Dev team) and ceremonies.

entries.question: What is Kanban?
entries.answer: **Kanban** — Visual board with work-in-progress limits; continuous flow.
entries.summary: Kanban — Visual board with work-in-progress limits; continuous flow.

entries.question: What is Sprint?
entries.answer: **Sprint** — Fixed time box (usually 2 weeks) to deliver work.
entries.summary: Sprint — Fixed time box (usually 2 weeks) to deliver work.

entries.question: What is Scrum Ceremonies?
entries.answer: **Scrum Ceremonies** — Sprint Planning, Daily Stand-up, Sprint Review (demo), Retrospective.
entries.summary: Scrum Ceremonies — Sprint Planning, Daily Stand-up, Sprint Review (demo), Retrospective.

entries.question: What is Backlog?
entries.answer: **Backlog** — Prioritised list of work items.
entries.summary: Backlog — Prioritised list of work items.

entries.question: What is Epic / Story / Task / Bug?
entries.answer: **Epic / Story / Task / Bug** — Large goal / user-facing requirement / technical step / defect.
entries.summary: Epic / Story / Task / Bug — Large goal / user-facing requirement / technical step / defect.

entries.question: What is User Story?
entries.answer: **User Story** — "As a <user>, I want <goal>, so that <benefit>."
entries.summary: User Story — "As a , I want , so that ."

entries.question: What is Acceptance Criteria?
entries.answer: **Acceptance Criteria** — Conditions a story must meet to be accepted.
entries.summary: Acceptance Criteria — Conditions a story must meet to be accepted.

entries.question: What is Definition of Done (DoD)?
entries.answer: **Definition of Done (DoD)** — Team checklist for when work is truly complete.
entries.summary: Definition of Done (DoD) — Team checklist for when work is truly complete.

entries.question: What is Story Points / Velocity?
entries.answer: **Story Points / Velocity** — Relative effort estimate / points a team completes per sprint.
entries.summary: Story Points / Velocity — Relative effort estimate / points a team completes per sprint.

entries.question: What is SAFe (Scaled Agile Framework)?
entries.answer: **SAFe** (Scaled Agile Framework) — Agile for many teams; uses PI (Program Increment) planning.
entries.summary: SAFe (Scaled Agile Framework) — Agile for many teams; uses PI (Program Increment) planning.

entries.question: What is ITIL?
entries.answer: **ITIL** — IT service management framework: incidents, problems, changes.
entries.summary: ITIL — IT service management framework: incidents, problems, changes.

entries.question: What is Incident / Problem / Change?
entries.answer: **Incident / Problem / Change** — Outage to fix now / its root cause / controlled update (ITIL).
entries.summary: Incident / Problem / Change — Outage to fix now / its root cause / controlled update (ITIL).

entries.question: What is RCA (Root Cause Analysis)?
entries.answer: **RCA** (Root Cause Analysis) — Finding the real cause of an issue (e.g. 5 Whys).
entries.summary: RCA (Root Cause Analysis) — Finding the real cause of an issue (e.g. 5 Whys).

entries.question: What is Postmortem?
entries.answer: **Postmortem** — Blameless review after an incident with action items.
entries.summary: Postmortem — Blameless review after an incident with action items.

entries.question: What is On-Call?
entries.answer: **On-Call** — Rotation where an engineer responds to production alerts.
entries.summary: On-Call — Rotation where an engineer responds to production alerts.

entries.question: What is Runbook / Playbook?
entries.answer: **Runbook / Playbook** — Step-by-step guide for operational tasks or incidents.
entries.summary: Runbook / Playbook — Step-by-step guide for operational tasks or incidents.

entries.question: What is Forward Deployed Engineering?
entries.answer: **Forward Deployed Engineering** — Model where engineers work inside customer teams to deploy the product; see FDE role.
entries.summary: Forward Deployed Engineering — Model where engineers work inside customer teams to deploy the product; see FDE role.

entries.question: What is AI-Native Company?
entries.answer: **AI-Native Company** — Company whose product and workflows are built around AI from day one.
entries.summary: AI-Native Company — Company whose product and workflows are built around AI from day one.

entries.question: What is CAIO (Chief AI Officer)?
entries.answer: **CAIO** (Chief AI Officer) — Executive responsible for AI strategy and governance.
entries.summary: CAIO (Chief AI Officer) — Executive responsible for AI strategy and governance.

entries.question: What is Product Company vs Service Company?
entries.answer: **Product Company vs Service Company** — Builds its own product (Google, Zoho) vs builds for clients (TCS, Infosys, Accenture).
entries.summary: Product Company vs Service Company — Builds its own product (Google, Zoho) vs builds for clients (TCS, Infosys, Accenture).

entries.question: What is Startup / MNC / GCC?
entries.answer: **Startup / MNC / GCC** — Early-stage company / multinational / Global Capability Centre (offshore in-house unit).
entries.summary: Startup / MNC / GCC — Early-stage company / multinational / Global Capability Centre (offshore in-house unit).

entries.question: What is Onsite / Offshore?
entries.answer: **Onsite / Offshore** — Working at client location / from a remote delivery centre.
entries.summary: Onsite / Offshore — Working at client location / from a remote delivery centre.

entries.question: What is Client / Stakeholder?
entries.answer: **Client / Stakeholder** — Who pays / anyone affected by or influencing the project.
entries.summary: Client / Stakeholder — Who pays / anyone affected by or influencing the project.

entries.question: What is BRD / FRD / SRS?
entries.answer: **BRD / FRD / SRS** — Business / Functional / Software Requirements documents.
entries.summary: BRD / FRD / SRS — Business / Functional / Software Requirements documents.

entries.question: What is SOW (Statement of Work)?
entries.answer: **SOW** (Statement of Work) — Contract describing scope, deliverables and timelines.
entries.summary: SOW (Statement of Work) — Contract describing scope, deliverables and timelines.

entries.question: What is RFP / RFI / RFQ?
entries.answer: **RFP / RFI / RFQ** — Request for Proposal / Information / Quotation from vendors.
entries.summary: RFP / RFI / RFQ — Request for Proposal / Information / Quotation from vendors.

entries.question: What is T&M vs Fixed Price?
entries.answer: **T&M vs Fixed Price** — Billing by time spent vs fixed cost for fixed scope.
entries.summary: T&M vs Fixed Price — Billing by time spent vs fixed cost for fixed scope.

entries.question: What is KPI / OKR?
entries.answer: **KPI / OKR** — Key metric / Objectives & Key Results goal framework.
entries.summary: KPI / OKR — Key metric / Objectives & Key Results goal framework.

entries.question: What is ROI (Return on Investment)?
entries.answer: **ROI** (Return on Investment) — Benefit gained compared to cost.
entries.summary: ROI (Return on Investment) — Benefit gained compared to cost.

entries.question: What is Bench?
entries.answer: **Bench** — Service-company term: employee not yet assigned to a project.
entries.summary: Bench — Service-company term: employee not yet assigned to a project.

entries.question: What is Appraisal / Hike / Band?
entries.answer: **Appraisal / Hike / Band** — Performance review / salary increase / salary-grade level.
entries.summary: Appraisal / Hike / Band — Performance review / salary increase / salary-grade level.

entries.question: What is CTC (Cost to Company)?
entries.answer: **CTC** (Cost to Company) — Total yearly cost of an employee (salary + benefits).
entries.summary: CTC (Cost to Company) — Total yearly cost of an employee (salary + benefits).

entries.question: What is LPA (Lakhs Per Annum)?
entries.answer: **LPA** (Lakhs Per Annum) — Indian salary unit: 1 LPA = ₹1,00,000 per year. 100 LPA = 1 Crore.
entries.summary: LPA (Lakhs Per Annum) — Indian salary unit: 1 LPA = ₹1,00,000 per year. 100 LPA = 1 Crore.

entries.question: What is Fixed vs Variable Pay?
entries.answer: **Fixed vs Variable Pay** — Guaranteed salary vs performance bonus that may not be paid in full.
entries.summary: Fixed vs Variable Pay — Guaranteed salary vs performance bonus that may not be paid in full.

entries.question: What is In-Hand Salary?
entries.answer: **In-Hand Salary** — Monthly amount after tax, PF and deductions — roughly 65–80% of fixed CTC ÷ 12.
entries.summary: In-Hand Salary — Monthly amount after tax, PF and deductions — roughly 65–80% of fixed CTC ÷ 12.

entries.question: What is ESOP / RSU?
entries.answer: **ESOP / RSU** — Stock options (startups) / restricted stock units (listed companies) given as part of pay.
entries.summary: ESOP / RSU — Stock options (startups) / restricted stock units (listed companies) given as part of pay.

entries.question: What is Joining Bonus / Notice Buyout?
entries.answer: **Joining Bonus / Notice Buyout** — One-time payment on joining / employer pays to cut your notice period short.
entries.summary: Joining Bonus / Notice Buyout — One-time payment on joining / employer pays to cut your notice period short.

entries.question: What is Notice Period?
entries.answer: **Notice Period** — Time you must serve after resigning — typically 30–90 days in India.
entries.summary: Notice Period — Time you must serve after resigning — typically 30–90 days in India.

entries.question: What is B2B / B2C?
entries.answer: **B2B / B2C** — Business sells to businesses / to consumers.
entries.summary: B2B / B2C — Business sells to businesses / to consumers.

entries.question: What is Go-Live?
entries.answer: **Go-Live** — The moment a system is released to real users.
entries.summary: Go-Live — The moment a system is released to real users.

entries.question: What is Hypercare?
entries.answer: **Hypercare** — Intensive support period right after go-live.
entries.summary: Hypercare — Intensive support period right after go-live.

entries.question: Working Abroad from India (checked 11 Oct 2026): Germany — Realistic
entries.answer:
**Latest (11 Oct 2026):** Oct 2026: IT specialists without a degree confirmed eligible for the Blue Card with 3+ yrs experience. 2026 threshold €45,934 for IT. No sponsor licence needed — any German employer can hire you.

**Blunt take:** The best odds in the West for Indian engineers. English-only jobs exist, but German B1+ roughly triples your options.

- **Visa rule:** Blue Card 2026: €50,700/yr, or €45,934.20 for IT/shortage jobs. Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) gives a job-search stay.
- **High demand roles:** Backend Developer (Java), Full Stack Developer, DevOps / Cloud / SRE, SAP / Salesforce / ServiceNow, Data Engineer, AI / LLM Engineer, Cybersecurity
- **Some demand:** QA / Test Automation (SDET), Frontend Developer, Mobile Developer, Data Scientist / ML Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), Business Analyst, Product Manager, Project / Delivery Manager
- **Official source:** https://www.make-it-in-germany.com/en/visa-residence/types/eu-blue-card

**How to get in (best route first):**

1. Apply directly to German companies — no sponsor licence is needed, so most can hire you
2. Filter job boards for 'English' + 'visa sponsorship' (see live feed below)
3. Get your degree checked on anabin, or rely on the 3-yrs-experience IT route
4. Start German now — B1 opens mid-size companies, not just startups
5. Opportunity Card only if you have savings: job-search on the ground

entries.question: Working Abroad from India (checked 11 Oct 2026): UAE (Dubai/Abu Dhabi) — Realistic
entries.answer:
**Latest (11 Oct 2026):** 2026: Golden Visa widened with an AI-specialist route (no local contract needed if income is high enough). Strong demand in AI and cloud.

**Blunt take:** The easiest move for Indians. Good tax-free pay, but no citizenship path, and packages vary wildly.

- **Visa rule:** No lottery: the employer sponsors your visa. Golden Visa (10-yr) for Level 1–2 tech roles with basic salary AED 30,000+/month.
- **High demand roles:** AI / LLM Engineer, Full Stack Developer, Backend Developer (Java), DevOps / Cloud / SRE, Cybersecurity, SAP / Salesforce / ServiceNow, Project / Delivery Manager, Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE)
- **Some demand:** Data Engineer, Data Scientist / ML Engineer, Mobile Developer, Frontend Developer, Business Analyst, Product Manager, QA / Test Automation (SDET)
- **Official source:** https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/residence-visas/golden-visa

**How to get in (best route first):**

1. Ask your Indian employer about Gulf client projects — the fastest, zero-risk route
2. Apply on LinkedIn and Bayt to product firms and banks, not just staffing agencies
3. Many people interview in person on a visit visa — budget 4–6 weeks if you try it
4. Negotiate basic salary high: it decides Golden Visa eligibility and end-of-service pay

2. Target Amsterdam scale-ups and fintech (Adyen, Booking, ING tech)
3. Internal transfer from an MNC office in India
4. Budget for housing before accepting — it eats offers

**Blunt take:** EU HQs of big tech, all in English. Fewer openings than Germany, and Dublin rents are brutal.

- **Visa rule:** €40,904/yr for listed ICT roles (software, security, data), or €68,911 for others. Residency (Stamp 4) after 2 years.
- **High demand roles:** Cybersecurity, DevOps / Cloud / SRE, Data Engineer, Backend Developer (Java), AI / LLM Engineer, Full Stack Developer
- **Some demand:** Product Manager, Frontend Developer, Data Scientist / ML Engineer, Business Analyst, Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE)
- **Official source:** https://enterprise.gov.ie/en/what-we-do/workplace-and-skills/employment-permits/permit-types/critical-skills-employment-permit/

**How to get in (best route first):**

1. Internal transfer from Google/Microsoft/Salesforce/Stripe India to their Dublin HQs
2. Apply directly to Dublin HQ roles — your software/security/data role is on the critical-skills list
3. Referrals from Indian engineers already in Dublin

entries.question: Working Abroad from India (checked 11 Oct 2026): Remote for global companies — Moderate
entries.answer:
**Latest (11 Oct 2026):** 2026: fewer 'worldwide' roles than in 2021–22; most now require US/EU time-zone overlap.

**Blunt take:** No visa risk, but you compete with the whole world. Public proof of work matters more than your CV.

- **Visa rule:** Paid as a contractor or through an Employer of Record (Deel, Remote.com). Tax is paid in India.
- **High demand roles:** Full Stack Developer, AI / LLM Engineer, DevOps / Cloud / SRE, Frontend Developer, Mobile Developer
- **Some demand:** Backend Developer (Java), Data Engineer, QA / Test Automation (SDET), Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), Data Scientist / ML Engineer
- **Official source:** https://remotive.com/remote-jobs/software-dev

**How to get in (best route first):**

1. Build public proof: GitHub, a shipped product, technical writing
2. Apply only to roles open to India/APAC (live feed below)
3. Offer US/EU time-zone overlap — it removes the #1 objection
4. Start as a contractor; convert to full-time later
entries.summary: Latest (11 Oct 2026): 2026: fewer 'worldwide' roles than in 2021–22; most now require US/EU time-zone overlap.

entries.question: Working Abroad from India (checked 11 Oct 2026): Japan — Moderate
entries.answer:
**Latest (11 Oct 2026):** India–Japan HR partnership (Aug 2025) targets 50,000 skilled Indians over 5 years. Large IT shortage persists.

**Blunt take:** Big demand, lower pay than the West. Most jobs expect Japanese (JLPT N2).

- **Visa rule:** Engineer visa needs a degree or 10 yrs experience. HSP points can lead to PR in 1–3 years.
- **High demand roles:** Backend Developer (Java), Mobile Developer, QA / Test Automation (SDET), Full Stack Developer, DevOps / Cloud / SRE
- **Some demand:** Frontend Developer, AI / LLM Engineer, Data Engineer, SAP / Salesforce / ServiceNow
- **Official source:** https://www.isa.go.jp/en/applications/procedures/16-3.html

**How to get in (best route first):**

1. Learn Japanese to N3 → N2 — this is the real gate
2. Use Japan-focused placement programmes in India that hire directly
3. English-only roles: Rakuten, Mercari, PayPay, global firms in Tokyo
entries.summary: Latest (11 Oct 2026): India–Japan HR partnership (Aug 2025) targets 50,000 skilled Indians over 5 years. Large IT shortage persists.

entries.question: Working Abroad from India (checked 11 Oct 2026): Australia — Hard
entries.answer:
**Latest (11 Oct 2026):** Oct 2026: next 189 invitation round by 31 Oct. 185,000 PR places for 2026–27. ICT roles (software, BA, security, PM) on the long-term list. Sponsor threshold AUD 79,423 from 1 Jul 2026.

**Blunt take:** PR without a job is possible from India, but only with high points (age, PTE 79+, experience).

- **Visa rule:** Points-based PR (189/190) needs an ACS skills assessment and a high score. Employer sponsorship usually needs local presence.
- **High demand roles:** Backend Developer (Java), Full Stack Developer, Cybersecurity, Business Analyst, Project / Delivery Manager, Data Engineer, DevOps / Cloud / SRE
- **Some demand:** QA / Test Automation (SDET), Data Scientist / ML Engineer, AI / LLM Engineer, Frontend Developer, Product Manager
- **Official source:** https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/working-in-australia/skillselect

**How to get in (best route first):**

1. Get an ACS skills assessment
2. Max out English: PTE 79+ gives the biggest single points jump
3. Apply for state nomination (190) where ICT is listed
4. Employer sponsorship mostly after you're in the country

entries.question: Working Abroad from India (checked 11 Oct 2026): United Kingdom — Hard
entries.answer:
**Latest (11 Oct 2026):** Oct 2026 rule changes: no change to salary thresholds; new protections for sponsored workers. Market remains tight for mid-level.

**Blunt take:** Sponsors exist, but mid-level is crowded. Senior and niche skills get callbacks.

- **Visa rule:** £41,700/yr or the role's going rate, whichever is higher. The employer must hold a sponsor licence.
- **High demand roles:** AI / LLM Engineer, Cybersecurity, Data Engineer, DevOps / Cloud / SRE
- **Some demand:** Backend Developer (Java), Full Stack Developer, Data Scientist / ML Engineer, Product Manager, Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE)
- **Official source:** https://www.gov.uk/skilled-worker-visa

**How to get in (best route first):**

1. Internal transfer from a bank/consultancy GCC in India (Barclays, HSBC, LSEG, Accenture)
2. Apply only to firms on the official Register of Licensed Sponsors
3. Senior/specialist roles only — the salary floor rules out most junior offers
4. Global Talent visa if you have a strong public track record
entries.summary: Latest (11 Oct 2026): Oct 2026 rule changes: no change to salary thresholds; new protections for sponsored workers. Market remains tight for mid-level.

entries.question: Working Abroad from India (checked 11 Oct 2026): Singapore — Hard
entries.answer:
**Latest (11 Oct 2026):** EP minimum S$5,600/month in 2026, rising to S$6,000 from Jan 2027. Shortage roles (AI, cloud, security, data) earn bonus COMPASS points.

**Blunt take:** Getting harder. COMPASS gives fewer points when a firm already has many staff of your nationality.

- **Visa rule:** EP minimum salary (higher with age) plus 40 points on COMPASS.
- **High demand roles:** AI / LLM Engineer, Cybersecurity, Data Engineer, DevOps / Cloud / SRE
- **Some demand:** Backend Developer (Java), Full Stack Developer, Data Scientist / ML Engineer, Product Manager
- **Official source:** https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/employment-pass

**How to get in (best route first):**

1. Target shortage-list roles (AI, cloud, security, data) — they get bonus points
2. Choose firms with diverse teams; avoid Indian-heavy employers
3. Internal transfer to a regional HQ
entries.summary: Latest (11 Oct 2026): EP minimum S$5,600/month in 2026, rising to S$6,000 from Jan 2027. Shortage roles (AI, cloud, security, data) earn bonus COMPASS points.

entries.question: Working Abroad from India (checked 11 Oct 2026): Canada — Hard
entries.answer:
**Latest (11 Oct 2026):** 2026 levels plan: temporary foreign worker intake cut 37% (to 230,000). Software developers and data scientists are no longer on the Express Entry STEM list. Points for job offers are planned to return.

**Blunt take:** Much harder than in 2019–22. PR without a job needs a very high CRS, and the tech job market there is tight for newcomers.

- **Visa rule:** General Express Entry draws often need CRS 500+. Cybersecurity is still on the STEM list.
- **High demand roles:** Cybersecurity
- **Some demand:** Data Engineer, DevOps / Cloud / SRE, AI / LLM Engineer, Data Scientist / ML Engineer, Backend Developer (Java), Full Stack Developer
- **Official source:** https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry.html

**How to get in (best route first):**

1. Check your CRS on the official calculator first — below ~480, don't spend money
2. IELTS CLB 9+ is the cheapest big points boost
3. Watch provincial (PNP) tech streams
4. Intra-company transfer if your employer has a Canada office
entries.summary: Latest (11 Oct 2026): 2026 levels plan: temporary foreign worker intake cut 37% (to 230,000). Software developers and data scientists are no longer on the Express Entry STEM list. Points for job offers are planned to return.

entries.question: Working Abroad from India (checked 11 Oct 2026): United States — Very hard
entries.answer:
**Latest (11 Oct 2026):** H-1B is NOT stopped (no blanket suspension as of 9 Oct 2026). But: a Sept 18 executive order makes an employer's layoffs count against its H-1B petitions. On Oct 8, Microsoft, Adobe, TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL, Cognizant and Capgemini were suspended from green card sponsorship (PERM). The $100k H-1B fee is blocked in court. The lottery is now wage-weighted.

**Blunt take:** The hardest route right now. The classic Indian IT services path (TCS/Infosys/Wipro → H-1B → green card) just got much worse.

- **Visa rule:** Wage-weighted H-1B lottery since Feb 2026: higher offered wage = better odds.
- **High demand roles:** AI / LLM Engineer, Data Scientist / ML Engineer
- **Some demand:** Backend Developer (Java), Cybersecurity, Data Engineer, DevOps / Cloud / SRE, Full Stack Developer, Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE)
- **Official source:** https://www.uscis.gov/working-in-the-united-states/h-1b-specialty-occupations

**How to get in (best route first):**

1. L-1 transfer from a US product company's India office (not IT services) after 12+ months
2. A high-wage offer for a senior/AI role improves lottery odds under the new rules
3. O-1 if you have a strong public record (patents, talks, major open source)
4. US master's → OPT → H-1B: costly and slow, but still the most common path

entries.question: Working Abroad from India (checked 11 Oct 2026): How to Actually Get an Interview
entries.answer:
1. Internal transfer beats everything. Join an MNC/GCC in India with offices abroad, perform, and ask after 12–18 months.
2. Get a referral. Cold applications from India mostly go unread; message engineers at target companies with a short, specific ask.
3. Apply only where you can legally be hired. Check sponsor registers (UK, Netherlands) or pick countries with no licence rule (Germany).
4. Prepare like it's a product company: DSA, system design, behavioural rounds.
5. Learn the language where it's the gate: German B1+ or Japanese N2.
6. Use the local CV format: 1–2 pages, no photo or date of birth (UK/US/IE), numbers in every bullet.
7. A master's abroad works, but it's the most expensive route. Only do it with a clear job plan.
8. Never pay an agent for a job offer. That's a scam, every time.

entries.question: Who Does What in a Project
entries.answer:
| Phase | What | Who | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Requirement | Understand what the business needs. | Business Analyst, Product Manager/Owner, Client | BRD, user stories, acceptance criteria |
| 2. Design | Plan the architecture and user experience. | Architect, Tech Lead, UI/UX Designer | Architecture diagrams, wireframes, API contracts |
| 3. Development | Write and review the code. | Frontend, Backend, Full Stack, Mobile Developers | Source code, pull requests, unit tests |
| 4. Testing | Verify it works and is secure. | QA / SDET, Performance Tester, Security Engineer | Test cases, bug reports, test reports |
| 5. Deployment | Release to production. | DevOps / Release Engineer, Cloud Engineer | CI/CD pipeline, release notes, deployed build |
| 6. Operations & Support | Keep it running and fix issues. | SRE, Production Support, IT Support | Dashboards, alerts, incident & RCA reports |
| Throughout | Plan, track and remove blockers. | Scrum Master, Project/Delivery Manager, Engineering Manager | Sprint plans, status reports, risk logs |
